item.title: Russian Espionage Group Exploited Zimbra Zero-Day to Steal Mail and 2FA Codes
item.description:
A Russian state-supported espionage group spent months reading Western mailboxes through a then-unknown flaw in Zimbra's webmail client.
The payload goes after the last 90 days of email, the organization's entire email directory, the password saved in the browser and the codes kept for two-factor recovery. Opening the message was enough to start it.

item.title: N-day is Becoming N-Hour. Patching Faster Won't Save You.
item.description:
Every patch is a confession.
The moment a vendor ships a security fix, the diff between the old code and the new code tells anyone watching exactly what was broken and where. Turn that diff back into a working exploit, and you can hit every system that hasn't updated yet. This is N-day exploitation, and it's always been a race: the vendor patches, the clock starts, and defenders try to deploy
item.author: info@thehackernews.com (The Hacker News)
